items.basis: The spring-to-close mechanism fails to account for potential contamination-induced sticking in the pilot valve, which would prevent proper closure during power failure despite the spring return
The 8 bar operating pressure exceeds the typical pressure rating of standard spring-loaded drain valves, risking catastrophic failure during high-demand cycling
The candidate provides no evidence to support the claimed zero carryover prediction, while industry data shows similar systems typically experience carryover events at 5-8% of operating cycles
The design fails to address the primary failure mode of moisture separators (coalescing element saturation) which remains unchanged from the baseline
The capacitive level sensor cannot reliably detect condensate at 8 bar pressure due to dielectric constant variations under pressure, making the trigger mechanism unreliable
The 2-second closure measurement lacks specification of the pressure decay curve during closure, allowing for false positives where the valve appears closed but still allows leakage
